issue_context.title: Use collection helper in integrations that consume Home Assistant data
issue_context.body:
In https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/30313 I've extracted a set of [collection helpers](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/homeassistant/helpers/collection.py) based on how the [Person integration](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/person/__init__.py) is handling it's configuration:
 - Allow configuring static data via YAML
 - Allow configuration stored in storage, managed via websocket API CRUD commands
 - Make sure those collections don't have IDs that overlap

In #30493 the collection helper also added support for reloading YAML

We should add this new collection helper to other integrations that currently only work with configuration.

 - [x] Zone. Notes: remove config flow support. `async_setup_entry` -> import it into storage collection and remove entry. #30774
 - [x] Input Boolean #30514 
 - [x] Input DateTime #30815
 - [x] Input Number #30576
 - [x] Input Select #30604
 - [x] Input Text #30633 
 - [x] Timer #30765 

For each integration that is migrated, we'll add a management UI to manage the storage collection.
comments:
I'm open to ideas of a better way to handle the following situation with `input_datetime`
1. User creates a `input_datetime.entity_1` entity with `{"has_date": True, "has_time": False}`
2. entity is being used etc
3. User/collection sends a WS Update for `input_datetime.entity_1` with `{"has_date": False, "has_time": True}` update fields

This update is going to break the entity, unless the entity is reset.  One way or another the state is going to be affected.

I was thinking about: modifying `input_datetime` so internally it is always a date+time  stamp, but state is formatted accordingly to `has_date` and `has_time`. But transitions from date only to time only or vice versa are still going to be ugly, until the value is set by the user.

Ignoring the update (saving, but not applying to existing entity) seems user unfriendly. 
Any other ideas?
Is there anything left to do here?
I don't think there's anything left on the back end side. Closing this for now.

review_comments: I wonder if we should add this to the collection helper in a future PR. We're going to add it everywhere ?

I also wouldn't mind if the `Child` class attach the `_collection_changed` method automatically if one exists.
well it's one or the other 👍
